title: Nvidia-Backed Firmus Sought $30B Valuation on $51M Revenue
source_used: Taipei Times page carrying a Bloomberg report (read in full); Briefs Finance for context
key_facts: Firmus Grid Ltd abandoned one of Australia's biggest-ever initial public offerings after investors balked at AI valuations; the deal would have valued it at US$30 billion, up from US$10.5 billion less than three months earlier.
Firmus had revenue of US$51 million in the 2026 financial year and no proven track record, which made the steep valuation hard to sell.
It was seeking to raise as much as US$5.5 billion including a greenshoe option; it will withdraw its ASX application and consider other funding, including a possible US listing in the longer term.
Its pipeline is 912 megawatts of data-center capacity, of which only 46 megawatts has been built, according to investor documents seen by Bloomberg.
The board said the terms on which the offer could proceed 'would not appropriately reflect the strength of the company's business'.
Analyst Josh Gilbert of eToro said investors would not pay a high price up front for capacity still largely on the drawing board, and higher yields lifted borrowing costs.
Nearly US$500 billion of new debt has been priced this year to fund AI infrastructure.
quote_evidence: Firmus Grid Ltd abandoned its attempt at one of Australia’s biggest-ever initial public offerings, after the Nvidia Corp-backed data center company failed to lure global investors who have grown increasingly skittish over frothy AI valuations.

Part of the difficulty was convincing potential investors of the steep increase in market value for a company without a proven track record that had revenue of US$51 million in the 2026 financial year.
It has a pipeline of 912 megawatts, of which only 46MW has been built, according to investor documents seen by Bloomberg.
why_it_matters_hint: A heavily backed AI data-centre firm could not sell shares at a $30 billion price on $51 million of revenue.
